To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the as-prepared Mo-doped cuprate is a SG system and the SC phase is formed by oxygenation of the material.
the Mo0.3Ca0.7SrCu2Oy system is a new SG system and that it can be converted into a SC material by an oxygen annealing process.
we have found the first example of a spin glass (TSG = 6 K) to superconducting (TSC,onsets = 31 K) transformation by oxidation in cuprates.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed study of the structural, magnetic and superconducting properties of the Mo0.3Ca0.7Sr1−yTm2−yCu2Oy compound, which is a member of the family of molybdo cuprates.
the synthesis, structure, and properties of the Mo0.3Sr2Tm0.5Cu2Oy system and the influence of oxygen annealed in the structure and superconducting properties.
the structural and magnetic properties of the Mo0.3Sr2Tm1.5Cu2.3Oy compound and its evolution upon oxygen annealing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Mo0.3Ca0.7Sr1.6Y0.4Cu2Oy sample is a SG material for the as-prepated sample and a superconductor for the annealed sample, with the SC phase being the result of an oxidation process.
the oxygen annealing of the as-prepared Mo–Cu–Sr–Cu–O system leads to the transformation from SG to SC.
the oxygen annealed Mo-substituted cuprate is superconducting with TSC,onset =31 K.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are reporting a new class of superconducting material that is prepared by oxidation of a SG material.
the Mo ions in the as-prepared MoCuSr2Tm2Oy material are distributed in the CuO2 planes and in the CuO1.5 planes.
the Mo0.3Sr2Tm0.2Cu2Oy system exhibits a spin glass to superconductivity transformation on oxidation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oxygenation reaction can be used to tune the physical properties of a material.
a Mo substitution for Cu is found to induce a spin glass state, which is transformed into a superconducting state following an oxygen annealing process.
a SG–SC phase transformation can be achieved by a chemical reaction in cuprate superconductors.
